page: Vultr vcg-a40-12c-60g-24vram is a virtual machine in the Cloud GPU family, featuring a fractionalized NVIDIA A40 GPU based on the Ampere architecture. This configuration provides 0.5 of a physical GPU, delivering 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 12 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. System memory totals 60.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 5.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as a 1110 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the average tier across most standard compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1631.08, while the multi-core score reaches 20624.31. Memory bandwidth testing shows a read-only small block cached speed of 1186.32 GB/sec, which drops to 123.01 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write speed of 53.08 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance achieves 22.59 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a Passmark database score of 5563.82.

The shared CPU allocation introduces potential performance variability under sustained compute-heavy workloads. This tradeoff is reflected in LLM inference benchmarks; while prompt processing for a small 135M model reaches 1048.4 tokens/sec, processing for a medium 7B model drops to a weak score of 23.45 tokens/sec, though text generation for the 7B model remains average at 9.43 tokens/sec. Given the 24 GB VRAM and 1110 GB NVMe storage, this instance is suitable for small-to-medium machine learning inference, data science prototyping, and database operations that benefit from GPU acceleration without requiring a full dedicated GPU.
